panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: Axial contrast CT of a real patient from an XGP-focused article; the in-text states XGP is staged by the Malek classification and points to this figure. Panel a shows an obstructing left renal-pelvic staghorn calculus with grade IV hydronephrosis (Malek I, disease confined to the kidney) — the hallmark CT presentation of XGP. Only panel letter 'a' is present; no diagnostic arrows/callouts. Hydronephrosis is not in the vocabulary, so it is proposed. b: Axial CT of a real patient in the XGP article; caption and in-text tie it to Malek III (extension into perinephric/retroperitoneal space). Panel b shows retroperitoneal collections surrounding the right kidney with a renal pelvic calculus, i.e. perirenal inflammatory extension of XGP — a recognized, more advanced/diffuse form (variant) rather than the confined focal presentation. Only panel letter 'b' is present; no diagnostic arrows/callouts.

panels.figure_caption: Xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis Stage I—nephritic form. CT with contrast agent: axial (a,b) and coronal MPR reconstruction (c). The left kidney is increased in volume with a characteristic “contracted” appearance of the renal pelvis. The renal parenchyma is extremely thinned and characterized by the presence of multiple hypodense areas representing both intraparenchymal collections of pus and dilated calyces. The wall of the pyelocaliceal structures is thickened and hyperemic due to granulation tissue and parenchymal compression caused by abscess cavities. Staghorn lithiasis is present. Perirenal fat is thickened but no peri- or pararenal collections are present. No fistulas or abscesses are evident. The characteristic “bear paw sign” and contracted appearance of the pelvis allowed for the diagnosis of XGP, confirmed on histologic examination. The “bear paw sign” was appreciated on the CT scan in 66.67% of patients.
in_text_mentions: suspected urothelial carcinoma, the delayed phase can be acquired in the prone position. CT exams were retrospectively reviewed in a consensus reading by two radiologists with experience in abdominal radiology (FP, MS) and a radiologist with experience in urological radiology (ST). CT imaging findings of lithiasis, staghorn calculi, hydro- and pyonephrosis, the presence of blood or air in the collecting system, a “bear paw sign”, xanthomas, fat stranding, abscess, pleural effusion, fistulization, and adherence to surrounding structures (Figure 1, Figure 2, Figure 3 and Figure 4) were recorded.

isease was 94.4% (40/41) and was indeterminate in 5.6% (1/41). In one case, a focal lesion with undefined margins and corticomedullary extension was reported as indeterminate. The patient underwent PET-CT examination that showed the absence of FDG uptake and a nephron-sparing surgery was performed; the final histologic diagnosis was a focal form of XPG. CT findings in the three different stages of XGP were reported; fistulization was a typical finding of XGP in stage III, although the sample size did not allow for inferential conclusions (Table 4 and Figure 3, Figure 4, Figure 5 and Figure 6).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (a, b, c, d). a: Axial contrast-enhanced CT in a patient with stage III xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis, showing right renal staghorn calculus and perirenal/pararenal inflammatory changes. b: Axial contrast-enhanced CT in a patient with stage III xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis, showing right renal staghorn calculus and posterior inflammatory extension into the psoas muscle. c: Coronal MPR contrast-enhanced CT in stage III xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis, showing right renal staghorn calculus and an inferior polar collection extending across the perirenal fascia. d: Sagittal MPR contrast-enhanced CT in stage III xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis, showing right renal staghorn calculus and peri/pararenal inflammatory changes.

panels.figure_caption: Xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis Stage III—pararenal form CT with contrast agent: axial (a,b), coronal (c), and sagittal (d) MPR reconstruction. In the right kidney, staghorn lithiasis is present; gross vesical lithiasis is also visible. The walls of the ureter are thickened and hyperemic. The CT was performed after nephrostomy placement, so significant calico-pyelic dilatation is not significant. Peri- and pararenal collections are evident, particularly the inferior polar collection (c) that passes the perirenal fascia. Posteriorly (b), the inflammatory process passes and infiltrates the psoas muscle. The staghorn lithiasis, the coexistence of calico-pyelic dilatation and fluid collections, and especially, the high invasiveness of the pathology, allowed, with high diagnostic confidence, to make the diagnosis of XGP.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: H&E photomicrograph of a patient nephrectomy specimen showing renal parenchyma replaced by sheets of lipid-laden foamy macrophages, the classic histologic hallmark of xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis, explicitly attributed to XGP by the caption and disease-focused article title. Blue arrows annotate the parenchymal and xanthomatous areas. B: High-power H&E view of the same nephrectomy specimen showing sheets of polygonal foamy macrophages (xanthoma cells) with admixed lymphocytes, the classic microscopic presentation of xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis, directly attributed to XGP in the caption. Lymphocytic infiltrate noted on the image is not in the allowed vocabulary and is recorded as a proposed finding.
panels.attribution_text: Fazal et al. Laparoscopic nephrectomy for Xanthogranulomatous Pyelonephritis: First surgical outcomes report from Pakistan.. Pakistan journal of medical sciences 2026. doi:10.12669/pjms.42.(11aasc).15801. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Photomicrograph of the one of the laparoscopic nephrectomy specimens exhibiting renal parenchyma (Fig2a →), partly replaced by sheets of macrophages (Fig 2a↓). High power image (40X, Fig 2b) depicts polygonal macrophages with abundant foamy cytoplasm due to deposition of lipids (xanthoma cells). Admixed lymphocytes are also seen. These macrophages are positive of CD68 (not shown here). These findings are consistent with Xanthogranulomatous Pyelonephritis (H&E, 10X & 40X).
in_text_mentions: over the world. 7 Xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis (XGPN) was first described by Schlagenhaufer in 1916 as “Staphylomycosis”.8 It closely mimics renal cell carcinoma clinically, macroscopically and microscopically.9 It is marked by progressive destruction of the renal parenchyma, replaced by granulomas, abscesses, and clusters of lipid-laden macrophages (Fig.2).10 The inflammation has zonal pattern with bacteria, inflammatory cells seen in the inner most zone, surrounded by lipid laden macrophages. The outermost zone shows giant cells, cholesterol clefts and fibrosis with lymph aggregates.9

panels.rationale: Single axial noncontrast abdominal CT (panel A) from an article titled 'Xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis with psoas abscess and renocolic fistula.' The caption states a marked thinning of the right renal cortex and large staghorn calculi filling the middle calyces in both kidneys; the bright central renal calculi are visible on the image. The combination of an obstructing central staghorn calculus with renal cortical thinning, in a disease-focused XGP article, supports attribution to XGP. This is a noncontrast study, so the contrast-dependent bear's paw sign is not applicable; no subtype is stated in the caption or title.

in_text_mentions: We describe a case of a 46-year-old woman with bilateral staghorn stones and end-stage renal disease (ESRD) under renal replacement therapy by hemodialysis. An abdominal CT scan suggested bilateral XGP (Figure 1) and she was submitted to bilateral nephrectomy. Histopathological analysis confirmed the diagnosis.

panels.rationale: Single axial abdominal-pelvic CT (panel A) of a 25-year-old woman (image metadata: born 18-08-1985, scanned 19-01-2011) from an article focused on xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis in pregnancy. The caption and in-text describe a dilated collecting system with a 55 mm coraliform (staghorn) calculus in the renal pelvis, and the image shows the corresponding central calculus with radiating dilated calyceal cavities (bear's paw appearance) in an enlarged right kidney—classic CT manifestations of XPN. Disease attribution rests on the disease-focused article title together with the specific captioned staghorn-calculus/dilated-collecting-system manifestation and the prior caption triage (route keep); a staghorn calculus alone is not exclusive to XPN, so confidence is moderated. The in-text phrase '1 month after birth' is tied to Figure 1 and conflicts with the visible 25-year-old metadata and the pregnancy context, so age is taken as adult.

The urine culture showed Proteus mirabilis growth. Contrasted computed tomography of the abdomen (Figure 1b) showed a 1.6 cm pelvic staghorn calculus, marked calyceal dilatation and paradoxical pelvic contraction in the left kidney, in addition to diffuse hypodensity and hypoenhancement of the renal parenchyma, which gave the standard image of a "bear paw".

panels.rationale: Coronal contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis in a human patient demonstrates the classic CT triad of xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis: an enlarged, architecturally distorted left kidney with a central hyperdense staghorn calculus, multiple contiguous hypodense abscesses/cavitary destruction (bear's-paw appearance), and surrounding inflammatory change. The yellow arrow indicates the renocolic fistula to the splenic flexure, which is explicitly described in the in-text mention and article title. Caption and in-text directly attribute the imaging to XGP, and the prior caption-triage route is keep. No skin, ethnicity, or age information is provided.

The patient underwent exploratory laparotomy, takedown and repair of renocolic fistula, partial omentectomy, and left nephrectomy by urology and general surgery teams. The patient had an uncomplicated postoperative course and was discharged home on postoperative day six with stable hemoglobin of 8 g/dL.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Axial contrast CT at the renal hila showing a swollen, poorly enhancing left kidney with calyceal distension (bear's paw appearance), cortical thinning, a high-attenuation renal pelvis calculus, and perirenal inflammatory stranding. The caption explicitly attributes these appearances to left-sided xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis, and the article title and in-text mentions confirm XGP. B: Axial contrast CT just inferior to the left kidney showing rim-enhancing low-attenuation abscesses in the enlarged left psoas and iliacus muscles, with a fleck of calcification (extruded calculus) in the psoas abscess. The caption states these appearances are consistent with left-sided xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis and secondary abscess formation, representing extra-renal inflammatory extension of XGP.

Clinical nephrology. Case studies 2015. doi:10.5414/cncs108594. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Axial CT source images. A: At the level of the renal hila. The swollen left kidney enhances poorly following intravenous contrast administration. There is calyceal distension and overlying cortical thinning. High attenuation calculus material is seen in the renal pelvis (white arrows). There is inflammatory stranding in the pararenal fat. B: Just inferior to the left kidney. Well-defined, low attenuation lesions are seen in both the enlarged left psoas and iliacus muscles (white arrows); the former contains a fleck of calcification. The rim of both lesions enhances with the administered intravenous contrast. Appearances are consistent with left-sided xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis and secondary abscess formation. The psoas abscess contains an extruded calculus.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Sagittal CT from a confirmed XGP case showing staghorn calculus, dilated calyces (bear's paw pattern), parenchymal atrophy and enlarged distorted kidney; caption and in-text explicitly attribute these findings to xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis. B: Coronal CT from a confirmed XGP case showing central staghorn calculus, markedly dilated calyces (bear's paw sign), parenchymal atrophy and exuberant fibrofatty proliferation; caption and in-text explicitly attribute these findings to xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis with extensive lipomatosis.

Computed tomography (CT) images showed obstructive stone, dilated calyces and renal parenchymal atrophy with exuberant fibrofatty proliferation (Figures 2 and 3). Final diagnosis was xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis with extensive lipomatosis.

in_text_mentions: On pathological examination, Xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis (XGP) was diagnosed. On microscopic examination, there is the focal replacement of renal parenchyma by severe mixed inflammatory cells infiltration including lymphoplasma cells, neutrophils and foamy histiocytes infiltration, and fibrosis with extension to perirenal soft tissue. Diabetic nephropathy including nodular sclerosis and arteriolar hyalinosis is seen in the background (Figure 4).

panels.rationale: Coronal delayed CT urogram from a case report of simultaneous upper-tract urothelial carcinoma and XGP. The right kidney shows a central staghorn calculus, perirenal inflammatory stranding, enlargement with no excretion, and cortical thinning — classic CT features of xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis. The left kidney excretes normally, serving as an internal comparison. Disease attribution is supported by the article title and in-text description of perirenal inflammatory stranding, calcification, and hydronephrosis.

panels.rationale: Single-panel abdominal radiograph from an article focused on xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis (XGP); the caption and in-text explicitly state the image demonstrates a right renal staghorn calculus in a patient whose final diagnosis was XGP. A central staghorn calculus is a classic manifestation of XGP (infection stone with chronic obstruction), so disease attribution is supported by the disease-focused article title plus the specific captioned finding. The image is a real patient radiograph with an arrow annotation pointing to the branching radiopaque calculus in the right renal fossa.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: High-power H&E from the nephrectomy specimen shows the classic foamy histiocytic infiltrate of xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis, supported by the caption and the article's histopathology description. B: High-power H&E shows the mixed histiocytic and neutrophilic inflammatory infiltrate described in the nephrectomy histopathology of xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis; the neutrophil microabscess component is not in the allowed vocabulary, so it is proposed rather than tagged. C: Low-power H&E from the same nephrectomy specimen shows diffuse histiocytic replacement of renal parenchyma, a classic histologic pattern of xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis. D: The red-arrowed multinucleated giant cell on H&E is a classic xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis histologic feature and is captured by the allowed Touton giant-cell finding; the caption and in-text description support attribution.

Based on these findings, a decision was made to finish the antimicrobial treatment and perform a radical right nephrectomy with the corresponding histopathological analysis of the removed material. The report described renal parenchyma with areas of fibrosis, sclerosis, and a lymphohistiocytic inflammatory infiltrate. Plasmocytes, foamy histiocyte accumulation, giant multinucleated cells, and an inflammatory infiltrate of polymorphonuclear neutrophils forming microabscess were evident as well (Figures 2, 3). These findings confirmed the diagnosis of xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis.

panels.rationale: Volume-rendered arterial-phase CT 3D reconstruction (anterior and lateral views of one figure, no panel letters) from a human patient in a case report of xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis. The caption explicitly documents left renal stones (purple arrow) consistent with staghorn lithiasis and a double-J stent (green arrow); the in-text radiology report describes a left renal inflammatory process on staghorn lithiasis with adhesive perirenal extension involving the posterior peritoneum, psoas and diaphragm, which fits XGP. Real patient radiology image, annotated with colored arrows, no third-party restriction, no competing disease attribution.

in_text_mentions: A CT was performed after correlating the clinical and laboratory findings to examine the thorax, abdomen, and pelvic regions. The imagistic report included a left renal inflammatory process more likely developed on untreated staghorn lithiasis. Important adhesion processes occurred between the kidney and the surrounding structures and altered the normal anatomy of the posterior peritoneum, psoas muscle, and left diaphragm. The relation between the kidney and the surrounding organs and the lithiasis pathology is reflected in Figure 1 and Figure 2.

panels.rationale: Coronal CT of a real patient showing the right kidney with significant central calcification (consistent with staghorn calculus in the XGP context), upper ureteral narrowing with proximal hydronephrosis (blue arrow), and perirenal inflammatory fat stranding (red arrow). Perirenal inflammatory extension is a specific XGP manifestation directly supported by the caption and matching the allowed vocabulary. The article title includes xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis and the prior caption-triage route is keep. Confidence is tempered because the article describes simultaneous upper-tract urothelial carcinoma, so some findings could be shared, but the perirenal inflammatory stranding is characteristic of XGP.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: Human-patient H&E histopathology of resected renal/ureteric tissue in a disease-focused case report of xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis. Caption describes inflammatory infiltrates, ulceration, granulation tissue and microabscesses in the pyelocaliceal area and ureter; the in-text explicitly ties xanthomatous (foamy) histiocytes and multinucleated histiocytic giant cells to Figure 4, supporting the two histology vocabulary findings. b: Human-patient H&E histopathology showing inflammatory extension into perirenal adipose tissue, a recognized manifestation of xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis. Disease attribution is supported by the disease-focused article title together with the specific captioned perirenal manifestation. c: Human-patient H&E histopathology of renal parenchyma showing tubules with a pseudothyroid phenomenon and central intratubular microabscesses, as described in the caption of a xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis case...

panels.figure_caption: Anatomopathological details. Hematoxylin–eosin stain (HE). (a) Inflammatory infiltrates extended in the pyelocaliceal area and ureter. Area of ulceration, granulation tissue, and reactive epithelial modifications. Multiple polymorphonuclear neutrophiles with intraepithelial extension and microabscesses. HE-10x; (b) extension of the inflammatory process in the perirenal adipose tissue. HE-10x; (c) renal tubules with pseudo thyroid phenomena. In the center, intratubular microabscesses. HE-20x.
in_text_mentions: On microscopy, representative sections examined showed granulomatous mixed inflammatory cell infiltrate. Sheets/Aggregates/Nodules of xanthomatous histiocytes with an admixture of neutrophils, lymphocytes, and plasma cells in various numbers were seen—Figure 4. Multinucleated histiocytic giant cells were noteworthy. Areas of fibrosis were also observed.

plate_findings.evidence: rich in foamy histiocytes

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel A is a low-power H&E section of renal parenchyma extensively remodeled and destroyed by inflammatory infiltrate in a patient with confirmed xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis. The specific xanthogranulomatous foamy histiocyte finding is not explicitly captioned for this panel, so the main diagnostic features are proposed rather than vocabulary-mapped. B: Panel B is an H&E section showing fibro-adipose involution with a cell population rich in foamy histiocytes, a classic histologic finding in xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis; the caption directly supports the foamy xanthoma cell finding. C: Panel C is an H&E section showing cholesterol-rich clefts surrounded by a polymorphic inflammatory population rich in foamy histiocytes, consistent with xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis; the foamy histiocyte finding is directly captioned, while cholesterol clefts are proposed because they are not in the configured vocabulary.

panels.rationale: Coronal contrast-enhanced CT of abdomen/pelvis from a case report of xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis. The caption explicitly identifies a left renal calculus and a reno-gastric fistula, and the in-text describes perirenal fluid collections suspicious for abscesses with fistulous tracts to the gastric wall. The left kidney is enlarged and distorted with a bright central calculus and surrounding perirenal inflammatory change, consistent with XGP. The reno-gastric fistula is a recognized but uncommon complication, making this a variant presentation. No age, ethnicity, or skin findings are stated.

panels.rationale: Axial contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen in a human patient from a case report titled 'Xanthogranulomatous Pyelonephritis Causing Renocolic Fistula Presenting as Symptomatic Anemia.' The in-text explicitly attributes the findings to XGP: chronic left pyelonephritis with contiguous abscesses, a staghorn calculus 'concerning for XGP,' and a fistula between the left kidney and the splenic flexure (Figures 2-3). The visible staghorn calculus and the yellow arrow marking the renal/colon interface support the captioned renocolic fistula. The fistula itself is an unusual complication, so typicality is atypical; the renocolic fistula has no matching vocabulary key and is listed as a proposed finding.

in_text_mentions: elvis with contrast was performed and it revealed chronic left kidney pyelonephritis with multiple contiguous abscesses in the inferior left kidney with a staghorn calculus concerning for XGP; it also showed the fistula between the left kidney and the splenic flexure of the colon (Figures 2-3). The patient underwent exploratory laparotomy, takedown and repair of renocolic fistula, partial omentectomy, and left nephrectomy by urology and general surgery teams. The patient had an uncomplicated postoperative course and was discharged home on postoperative day six with stable hemoglobin of 8 g/dL.

in_text_mentions: tions of about 10 mm. In addition, a coralliform calculus measuring 85 × 34 × 40 mm within the collecting system was noted, thinning the wall and altering the architecture of the genitourinary system (Figure 2). Given the imaging findings, the patient was diagnosed with necrotizing pneumonia in the right lower lobe (RLL), in contact with the renal lesion on the same side. Initial management included empirical antibiotic therapy with ampicillin/sulbactam, which was later switched to piperacillin/tazobactam. Right renal exclusion was confirmed by scintigraphy after 13 days of antibiotic therapy.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: Axial CT of a human patient showing the classic XGP constellation: central staghorn calculus, calyceal ballooning (bear's paw sign), perinephric inflammatory stranding, and an enlarged distorted left kidney; the caption explicitly attributes these findings to xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis of the left kidney. b: Coronal CT of the same patient showing XGP of the left kidney with unusual superior extension into the splenic parenchyma, a subcapsular splenic collection, and trans-diaphragmatic spread causing a left pleural effusion; the caption attributes these changes to xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis, and the splenic/pleural extension is an uncommon presentation consistent with the case report title.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Coronal CT of the affected left kidney directly shows the textbook XGP combination of a bear’s paw pattern from dilated/multiloculated calyces with a central obstructive staghorn calculus. B: The CT is captioned as demonstrating XGP and shows an associated fluid-filled collection at the splenic hilum; the in-text describes additional abscesses at the splenic hilum in the same XGP patient, supporting attribution but as an uncommon associated finding. C: The article title states XGP presenting as a left-sided pleural effusion and the caption describes a moderate left pleural effusion with splenomegaly, making this an unusual but directly supported XGP presentation.

in_text_mentions: CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis was performed to investigate other potential sources of infection (Fig. 2). This demonstrated a chronic left pyelonephritis with a multiloculated appearance of the renal calyces, suggestive of XGP. There was also a large staghorn calculus obstructing the renal pelvis, with additional abscesses at the hilum of the spleen and inflammation of the tail of the pancreas.

in_text_mentions: An initial chest x-ray demonstrated no acute cardiopulmonary process. CT abdomen and pelvis revealed severe hydronephrosis and dilated calices of the left kidney with a 3.3 cm stone within the left renal pelvis along with stones in the lower poles of the left kidney. There was also gas within the left renal collecting system in the calices (Figures 1 and 2). The findings were concerning for XPN with emphysematous. The patient was transferred to inpatient care and treated with ceftriaxone 2.0 g IV q 24 h.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: H&E renal histology panel from the patient, caption explicitly labels it XGPN and shows sheets of foamy histiocytes replacing renal parenchyma. B: Higher-power H&E renal histology panel labeled XGPN, showing characteristic foamy histiocytes with central nuclei and abundant clear cytoplasm. C: H&E renal histology panel labeled XGPN, showing tubular thyroidisation and atrophy; this is a recognized XGPN histologic manifestation but the described features are not in the provided finding vocabulary.
panels.attribution_text: Daoud et al. Xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis mimicking renal cell carcinoma: a case report.. Annals of medicine and surgery (2012) 2023. doi:10.1097/ms9.0000000000000474. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: (A) XGPN, diffuse proliferation of foamy histiocytes replacing renal parenchyma with mixed inflammatory exudates. H&E×100. (B) XGPN, Foamy histiocytes with central nuclei and abundant clear cytoplasm. H&E×400. (C) XGPN, tubular thyroidisation (filled with colloid casts) and tubular atrophy. H&E×100.
in_text_mentions: To confirm the diagnosis; immune stains were recommended (Figs. 3 and 4). The suggested panel includes (CK, CK7, and CK20) and the suspected ‘clear cells’ were negative for CK, CK7, and CK20, which ruled out the diagnosis of RCC. The ‘foam cells’ consistent with XGPN were first misinterpreted as malignant ‘clear cells’. The immunohistochemistry study was essential to rule out malignancy and confirmed the diagnosis of XGPN. CD68 was not available in our pathology lab.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Gross specimen of the excised left kidney from a case of xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis (article title and in-text confirm nephrectomy for XGP); the enlarged, distorted renal contour is a classic gross manifestation of XGP. Real patient gross specimen, not a diagram or other disease. B: Cut surface of the nephrectomy specimen shows the classic gross triad of XGP: calculi in the pelvicalyceal system, yellowish/xanthomatous replacement of the parenchyma (in-text attributes yellowish discoloration to xanthoma cells), and loss of cortico-medullary differentiation. Real patient gross image, directly attributed to XGP by caption and disease-focused article title. C: Gross image of the extracted staghorn calculus from the excised kidney; staghorn calculus is the hallmark gross/radiologic finding of XGP and is directly captioned here. Real patient specimen image attributed to XGP by caption and article title.

in_text_mentions: n culture. After 5 days, a left-sided nephrectomy was performed, and the specimen was sent for histopathology examination. The surgical specimen weighed around 150 g (average 124g for female’s left kidney). The excised kidney measured 10.0 × 7.0 × 4.0 cm and was partially covered with perinephric fat. The attached ureter measured ~ 4.0 cm in length. The cut section of the kidney showed a staghorn calculus filling the pelvicalyceal system measuring 3.5 × 1.0 cm. Also, a few areas of yellowish discoloration were noted within the pelvicalyceal system, probably due to xanthoma cells (Figure 444C).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Axial contrast-enhanced CT shows a globally destroyed right kidney with stones, perinephric/paranephric inflammatory changes, and a right psoas abscess, marked by red and yellow arrows; the case is reported as XGPN. B: Sagittal contrast-enhanced CT reformation shows the same destroyed right kidney and adjacent inflammatory/psoas abscess findings in the reported XGPN case. C: Coronal contrast-enhanced CT shows the destroyed right kidney with calcifications, perinephric/paranephric inflammatory extension, and a large right psoas abscess in a case reported as XGPN.

panels.figure_caption: Contrast-enhanced abdominal computed tomography (CT) scan showing global destruction of the right kidney with extensive stones, perinephric/paranephric diffuse inflammatory changes, multiple spots of calcifications, and a large well-defined right psoas abscess. The red arrow represents a destroyed kidney with stones, and the yellow arrow shows pus collection.
in_text_mentions: Abdominal contrast CT findings are depicted in Figure 1. The CT scan was conclusive of a globally destroyed right kidney with replacement of its parenchyma with multiple low attenuation non-enhancing tissue. There are numerous large stones with several spots of calcifications and obvious perinephric and paranephric fat stranding. Furthermore, a large, well-defined right psoas fluid collection with wall enhancement represents an abscess. Based on the CT findings, the differential diagnosis included tuberculous pyelonephritis or XGPN.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: Genuine patient H&E histology from an XGP case showing necrotic, scaled urothelium of the renal pelvis and calyces, as stated in the caption. The described feature is not in the provided vocabulary, so it is recorded as a proposed finding; the panel still visibly shows a specific histopathologic manifestation of the target disease. [raw subtype: focal] b: Low-power H&E of the resected kidney from the XGP patient showing granulomatous inflammation with chronic inflammatory cell infiltration and focal abscess formation, as captioned. These features are not in the provided vocabulary and are recorded as proposed findings; the panel is genuine patient histopathology of the target disease. [raw subtype: focal] c: High-power H&E from the XGP patient showing sheets of lipid-laden xanthomatous (foamy) cells and multinucleated giant cells, directly matching two vocabulary histology findings and supporting the XGP diagnosis. panels.attribution_text: Ding et al. Atypical focal xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis without clinical symptoms presenting as infiltrative renal cancer: a case report and literature review.. BMC urology 2020. doi:10.1186/s12894-020-00632-3. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Microscopically, the majority of urothelium of the renal pelvis and calyceal is necrotic and scaled (a). At low power, the kidney shows a granulomatous inflammation with a large number of chronic inflammatory cell infiltration and focal abscess formation (hematoxylin-eosin, original magnification × 4) (b). At high power, the inflammatory infiltration is composed of a large number of lipid-laden xanthomatous cells, multinucleated giant cells, lymphoplasmacytic as well as some neutrophile cells (hematoxylin-eosin, original magnification × 40) (c)
in_text_mentions: a granulomatous inflammation with a large number of lipid-laden xanthomatous cells, multinucleated giant cells lymphoplasmacytic as well as some neutrophile cells, supporting a diagnosis of XGP (Fig. 2). Immunohistochemical examination was not necessary based on the typical pathological characteristics of hematoxylin-eosin staining. The patient recovered uneventfully after surgery. Ultrasound was performed every year and the patient went well at follow-up 3 year later. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Grayscale abdominal ultrasound showing a large staghorn calculus with posterior acoustic shadowing in a patient with XGP; the staghorn calculus is a classic imaging manifestation of xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis. B: Color Doppler ultrasound demonstrating the twinkling artifact from a staghorn calculus in an XGP patient; classic finding of central renal staghorn calculus in xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis. C: Ultrasound showing dilated proximal left ureter in close contact with a large collection in the left psoas region (psoas abscess), described in the article title as an unusual complication of XGP; represents inflammatory extension of the renal infection beyond the kidney.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Axial corticomedullary-phase CECT of a human patient showing an enlarged left kidney with dilated calyces and contracted renal pelvis (bear paw sign) plus a central staghorn calculus, a classic CT presentation of xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis explicitly named in the caption and article title. B: Coronal excretory-phase CECT of the same patient showing a large central staghorn calculus in the renal pelvis with additional calculi in the ureter and adjacent collection, directly supporting the XGP diagnosis stated in the caption. C: Coronal CECT showing a large left iliopsoas collection (psoas abscess) in the same patient, an inflammatory extension of the XGP process; the article title describes this as an unusual complication, so it is classified as atypical.

panels.figure_caption: Abdominal CECT axial and coronal section shows XGP of the left kidney. A – Corticomedullary phase of CECT shows an enlarged left kidney with gross hydroureteronephrosis with thinning of renal cortex and a staghorn calculus within the renal pelvis, which is contracted, whereas calyces are dilated giving the appearance of a “Paw of A Bear” (white arrow); B – Excretory phase of CECT shows a staghorn calculus measuring 3.8 × 2.4 cm (black arrow) within the renal pelvis. Multiple calculi, the largest measuring 1.6 × 1.4 cm (arrowheads), were noted in the ureter and the collection; C – Large collection within the left iliopsoas muscle consistent with left psoas abscess (white arrow).
in_text_mentions: The CECT depicted an enlarged left kidney with gross hydroureteronephrosis with thinning of the renal cortex and a staghorn calculus measuring ~ 3.8 × 2.4 cm within the renal pelvis. The renal pelvis appeared contracted, whereas calyces were dilated, giving the appearance of a “Paw of a Bear,” referred to as “Bear Paw Sign” (Figure 3A). Also, a large collection measuring 13.0 × 4.0 cm was found along the left iliopsoas muscle harboring multiple images consistent with calculi, the largest measuring ~1.6 × 1.4 cm (Figure 33C).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: Axial postcontrast CT of a human patient showing the classic bear's paw sign (dilated calyceal cavities) with cortical thinning and hypoperfusion of the left kidney; the caption directly attributes these findings to xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis. b: Coronal postcontrast CT reconstruction showing a ureteral stone in the distal left ureter; nephrolithiasis is a hallmark of XGPN and the in-text explicitly associates this figure with the staghorn calculus suspicious for XGPN. c: Oblique pyelogram after puncture of the inferior calix showing contrast leakage with a double fistulous path from the renal pelvis anteriorly to the left colon and posteriorly to the retroperitoneal collection; the article title and caption attribute this spontaneous renocolic fistula to the underlying XGPN with perinephric abscess, a recognized uncommon complication.
panels.attribution_text: Sforza et al. A Rare Case of Xanthogranulomatous Pyelonephritis with Spontaneous Renocolic Fistula and IVC Thrombosis.. Case reports in nephrology 2021. doi:10.1155/2021/3604017. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: (a) Postcontrast CT images showed hypoperfusion of the left kidney with thinning of the cortex; dilatation of the left kidney excretory system with a “bear's paw sign” is also depicted suggesting diagnosis of xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis (arrow); (b) postcontrast coronal reconstruction demonstrated ureteral stone (arrowhead) in the distal tract of the left ureter without significant dilatation of the proximal tract; (c) oblique projection pyelography after puncture of the inferior calix of the left kidney demonstrated leakage of contrast media with a double fistulous path form the pelvis directed anteriorly to the left colon (arrow) and posteriorly to the collection in the retroperitoneal collection (arrowhead).
in_text_mentions: Ultrasonography confirmed the diagnosis of DVT; a CT scan revealed pleural effusion, massive pulmonary embolism, inferior vena cava thrombosis, voluminous retroperitoneal abscess of the left psoas muscle and left kidney with irregular borders, hypodense areas, and a staghorn calculus suspicious for XGPN (Figures 1(a) and 1(b)).

After a multidisciplinary team meeting in the emergency area, the patient underwent an interventional radiologic procedure consisting of caval filter placement, left nephrostomy, and percutaneous drainage of the perinephric abscess; during the radiological procedure, contrast injected via the percutaneous drainage revealed a communication between the abscess, the lower pole calyx, and the descending colon (Figure 1(c)).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Low-power H&E of the left kidney from the XGP case shows parenchymal replacement by xanthogranulomatous inflammatory sheets with scattered giant cells; article title and in-text confirm XGP, and the in-text links these sections to sheets of histiocytes/foamy macrophages. B: High-power H&E shows sheets of foamy lipid-laden histiocytes (xanthoma cells), the textbook histologic hallmark of xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis, in the affected left kidney. C: High-power H&E confirms sheets of foamy xanthoma cells with lymphocytic aggregates, the defining histologic feature of XGP, in the left kidney of the reported case. D: High-power H&E of the same XGP kidney shows a hyalinized glomerulus and a thick-walled blood vessel, i.e. chronic parenchymal and vascular scarring accompanying the xanthogranulomatous destruction; supportive of XGP but nonspecific, so kept with moderate confidence and findings placed in proposed_findings.

panels.figure_caption: Photomicrographs of the left kidney. A – Microscopic section showing replacement of the renal parenchyma by sheets of acute and chronic inflammatory cells composed of neutrophils, lymphocytes, and plasma cells, scattered foreign body giant cells (H&E10X); B and C – Section shows sheets of polygonal histiocytes having abundant pale eosinophilic and foamy cytoplasm with a round nucleus and annexed with focal aggregates of lymphocytes (H&E 40X); D – Section shows the hyalinised glomeruli and thick-walled blood vessel (H&E 40X).
in_text_mentions: cally, the kidney sections showed hyalinized glomeruli and atrophic tubules lined by flattened cells, and the surrounding blood vessels were thickly walled. Interstitial fibrosis with a dense collection of inflammatory cells composed of sheets of lymphocytes, plasma cells, neutrophils, histiocytes, and multinucleated giant cells were seen. Islands of foamy macrophages, foci of calcification, lymphoid follicles, and thickened capsule were also seen. At some places, the inflammatory cells and the proliferating capillaries were overlined by a transitional epithelium with ulceration. (Figure 5AD).

panels.figure_caption: Xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis Stage III—pararenal form. Non-enhanced CT examination: axial (a,b) and coronal MPR reconstruction (c,d). The right kidney is increased in volume with reduced parenchymal representation and a “contracted” appearance of the renal pelvis. The renal parenchyma is extremely thinned and characterized by the presence of multiple hypodense areas that cannot be better characterized without contrast agent. (a) Within the fluid collection at the anterior middle third of the kidney, a “layer” characterized by fluid (white asterisk) and adipose density (above white asterisk) can be noted, named “xanthoma” and characteristic of the disease. Staghorn lithiasis is present. No significant thickening of the perirenal fat tissue is noted. On the posterior profile of the kidney, a fistulous via with hydro-gas content is visible ((a), white arrow; (b)), which carries posteriorly into the psoas and dorsal muscles with fluid collection in the context of the muscle bundles. The fistulous via terminates in the subcutaneous flank soft tissues where fluid collection with gas is present ((d), MPR coronal).
in_text_mentions: suspected urothelial carcinoma, the delayed phase can be acquired in the prone position. CT exams were retrospectively reviewed in a consensus reading by two radiologists with experience in abdominal radiology (FP, MS) and a radiologist with experience in urological radiology (ST). CT imaging findings of lithiasis, staghorn calculi, hydro- and pyonephrosis, the presence of blood or air in the collecting system, a “bear paw sign”, xanthomas, fat stranding, abscess, pleural effusion, fistulization, and adherence to surrounding structures (Figure 1, Figure 2, Figure 3 and Figure 4) were recorded.

isease was 94.4% (40/41) and was indeterminate in 5.6% (1/41). In one case, a focal lesion with undefined margins and corticomedullary extension was reported as indeterminate. The patient underwent PET-CT examination that showed the absence of FDG uptake and a nephron-sparing surgery was performed; the final histologic diagnosis was a focal form of XPG. CT findings in the three different stages of XGP were reported; fistulization was a typical finding of XGP in stage III, although the sample size did not allow for inferential conclusions (Table 4 and Figure 3, Figure 4, Figure 5 and Figure 6).

On the posterior profile of the kidney, a fistulous via with hydro-gas content is visible ((a), white arrow; (b)), which carries posteriorly into the psoas and dorsal muscles with fluid collection in the context of the muscle bundles. The fistulous via terminates in the subcutaneous flank soft tissues where fluid collection with gas is present ((d), MPR coronal).

panels.figure_caption: Xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis Stage III—pararenal form CT with contrast agent: axial (a,b,e), coronal (c), and sagittal (d) MPR reconstructions with lung window (e,f). Patient admitted for persistent cough and left basal opacity on chest X-ray examination. On CT examination, morpho-structural alteration of the kidney with gross intraparenchymal collections alternating with dilated calyces is present. An upper polar fistulous via (a,b) is well evident (white arrow) that continues into the lung in direct continuity with a bronchus, more evident in sagittal reconstructions. Recognition of the fistulous via on CT was visible in 22.22% of patients.
in_text_mentions: isease was 94.4% (40/41) and was indeterminate in 5.6% (1/41). In one case, a focal lesion with undefined margins and corticomedullary extension was reported as indeterminate. The patient underwent PET-CT examination that showed the absence of FDG uptake and a nephron-sparing surgery was performed; the final histologic diagnosis was a focal form of XPG. CT findings in the three different stages of XGP were reported; fistulization was a typical finding of XGP in stage III, although the sample size did not allow for inferential conclusions (Table 4 and Figure 3, Figure 4, Figure 5 and Figure 6).

panels.rationale: Single-panel H&E histopathology (200x) from a reported xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis case. The image and caption show the diagnostic histologic hallmark of XGP: sheets of lipid-laden (foamy) macrophages (thick arrow) with occasional multinucleate giant cells and dense chronic inflammatory cells (thin arrow), in a human patient specimen. Prior caption-triage confirms real patient image, no third-party copyright. Classic presentation; no subtype supported by the provided vocabulary. Age not stated in caption or in-text mentions, so age_group is unknown.

in_text_mentions: Histological evaluation revealed diffuse necrosis of the renal parenchyma and perinephric fat. Neutrophils, plasma cells, sheets of foamy macrophages and occasional multinucleate giant cells were seen (Figure 2). The renal vein was partially occluded by an inflammatory thrombus with fibrin, platelets and mixed inflammatory cells. The thrombus was focally adherent to the vein wall with thrombus. Adjacent areas showed histological features of chronic pyelonephritis.

in_text_mentions: Physical exam at presentation demonstrated a temperature of 38.3°C and a palpable left flank mass with overlying fluctuance. Laboratory evaluation demonstrated a hemoglobin of 8.5 g/dL and a white blood cell count of 18.6 × 103/μL with 84% segmented neutrophils. A voided urine culture was obtained which was later positive for E. coli. Abdominal CT demonstrated a chronically hydronephrotic left kidney with calcified debris within the collecting system and perinephric abscesses extending anterior and posterolateral to the kidney (Figure 1).

in_text_mentions: A CT was performed after correlating the clinical and laboratory findings to examine the thorax, abdomen, and pelvic regions. The relation between the kidney and the surrounding organs and the lithiasis pathology is reflected in Figure 1 and Figure 2.

in_text_mentions: thick perirenal fat, adhered to the peritoneum, with an intensely dilated pyelocalyceal system and filled with pus. panels.rationale: Axial contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen in a patient with confirmed xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis. The image shows an enlarged right kidney with multiple hypodense intrarenal collections (cavitary destruction), perirenal inflammatory extension, and an arrow indicating a fistulous tract from the upper pole of the right kidney to the duodenum. The renoduodenal fistula is a recognized but uncommon complication of XPN and is not represented in the allowed findings vocabulary, so it is placed in proposed_findings. Disease attribution is strongly supported by the caption, in-text description, and article title.

panels.rationale: Single axial contrast-enhanced abdominal CT of a pediatric patient from a case report of focal xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis in children. The image shows a large multiloculated, peripherally enhancing cavitary right renal mass with perirenal fat stranding, surgically confirmed as an abscess and histopathologically confirmed as focal XGP with foamy macrophages and granulomatous inflammation — specific manifestations of the configured target disease. No bear's paw sign or central staghorn calculus is described, so those keys are not tagged. The focal pediatric form with diagnostic uncertainty (abscess vs neoplasm) is a recognized less common presentation, hence variant typicality. Caption indicates a white arrow annotation. panels.rationale: Single axial contrast-enhanced CT from the XGP case report (real human patient radiology image; yellow arrow annotation present). The left kidney is enlarged and distorted by a large rim-enhancing fluid-filled cavitary lesion (caption: 'left renal mass with contrasted surface (arrow)'), fitting XGP cavitary/xanthomatous change in the obstructed (incomplete double ureter) kidney. Attribution to XGP rests on the case's final diagnosis after nephrectomy rather than on pathognomonic CT signs: no central staghorn calculus or classic bear's-paw calyces are seen on this slice, and the lesion was preoperatively misread as a cyst/renal cell carcinoma, so confidence is moderate and the tumor-like (focal) presentation is classed as variant. Not a diagram, animal, control, third-party, or other-disease comparison panel.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Axial CT showing left renal hydronephrosis, perirenal fat stranding, and calyceal distention in a patient with XGP. These are classic CT manifestations of XGP with perirenal inflammatory extension. B: Axial CT showing asymmetric enlargement of the left psoas muscle, representing perirenal inflammatory extension in XGP. Psoas involvement is a recognized but less common manifestation of XGP extension beyond the kidney. C: Axial CT showing a non-enhancing fat-containing lesion of the left kidney. Although initially interpreted as hemorrhagic angiomyolipoma, the final diagnosis in this case report is XGP presenting as spontaneous renal hemorrhage. The lesion represents cavitary destruction of renal parenchyma in XGP, an atypical imaging presentation.

in_text_mentions: Histopathology of the kidney showed nodular replacement of the renal parenchyma exhibiting a zonal pattern and central nidus of necrotic debris and neutrophils (microabscesses) with a mixture of inflammatory cells, including lymphocytes and plasma cells. The nidus was surrounded by sheets of lipid-laden macrophages with abundant clear cytoplasm (Figure 4), spindle-shaped fibroblasts, and multinucleated giant cells. The residual glomeruli were sclerotic, and the parenchymal arteries thickened.

in_text_mentions: Histopathological examination by Hematoxylin and Eosin stain (H&E) revealed xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis with extensive ischaemic necrosis. The pathognomonic microscopic feature is the lipid-laden foamy macrophage accompanied by both chronic- and acute-phase inflammatory cells as shown in the Figures 5-7. Real-time tuberculosis-polymerase chain reaction (TB-PCR) test was negative. Tissue culture showed no growth.

panels.rationale: Single H&E photomicrograph (100X) from the nephrectomy specimen of the reported XGPN case. Caption and in-text explicitly describe foamy macrophages with inflammatory infiltrate diffusely infiltrating renal parenchyma, the textbook histologic hallmark of xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis; the disease-focused article title and prior keep triage support attribution. No other disease is identified for this panel. The round thick-walled structures are vessels, not Touton giant cells, so only the foamy xanthoma cell finding is tagged; the accompanying inflammatory infiltrate is not in the vocabulary and is proposed.

panels.figure_caption: Microscopic examination at 100X magnification showing collection of foamy macrophages and inflammatory infiltrate diffusely infiltrating the renal parenchyma.
in_text_mentions: e paracaval lymph nodes. A provisional diagnosis of renal cell carcinoma with renal vein thrombus was made. The clinical stage was T3aN2M0. A laparoscopic radical nephrectomy was done. The gross specimen revealed evidence of renal vein thrombus and Xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis (XGPN) ( Figure 2). On H & E (Hematoxylin & Eosin) microscopic examination, it was composed of foamy macrophages admixed with inflammatory infiltrate ( Figure 3). There was no evidence of malignancy. The patient recovered well and was discharged in stable condition after 4 days with a serum creatinine of 1.16mg/dL.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Noncontrast axial CT of a real patient showing an enlarged left kidney with cystic/dilated pelvicalyceal spaces, a manifestation of xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis in an article specifically about that disease. B: Second noncontrast axial CT panel of the same real patient showing an enlarged left kidney with cystic/dilated pelvicalyceal spaces, supporting xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis in the disease-focused case report.

panels.figure_caption: A noncontrast computed tomography axial view of the abdomen showing the enlarged left kidney with cystic pelvicalyceal dilation.
in_text_mentions: A computed tomography (CT) scan of the abdomen and pelvis without contrast (Figs. 1 and 2) was performed and it showed an enlarged left kidney with cystic formation measuring 4×5 cm in maximum dimensions and dilation of the pelvicalyceal system with the presence of multiple variable-sized calculi. In addition, there was a large stone seen impacted at the proximal third of the ureter measuring 1.6 cm. The right kidney was normal in size and position.

plate_findings.evidence: in-text: foam cells consistent with XGPN were first misinterpreted as malignant clear cells; affected area is negative for cytokeratin, while residual renal tissue is positive

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel A is an immunohistochemistry image of kidney tissue from a XGPN case; the arrow highlights the affected area negative for cytokeratin, supporting the diagnosis by ruling out RCC. B: Panel B is an immunohistochemistry image of kidney tissue from a XGPN case; the arrow highlights the affected area negative for cytokeratin-7, supporting the diagnosis by excluding RCC. C: Panel C is an immunohistochemistry image of kidney tissue from a XGPN case; it shows the affected area negative for cytokeratin-20, supporting the diagnosis by ruling out RCC.
panels.attribution_text: Daoud et al. Xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis mimicking renal cell carcinoma: a case report.. Annals of medicine and surgery (2012) 2023. doi:10.1097/ms9.0000000000000474. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
panels.figure_caption: (A) Immunohistochemistry with cytokeratin (the arrow shows negativity for computed tomography in the affected area of the kidney) whereas the residual renal tissue is positive for computed tomography. (B) Immunohistochemistry with cytokeratin-7 (the arrow shows negativity for cytokeratin-7 in the affected area of the kidney). (C) Immunohistochemistry showing negativity for cytokeratin-20 in the affected area of the kidney.
in_text_mentions: To confirm the diagnosis; immune stains were recommended (Figs. 3 and 4). The suggested panel includes (CK, CK7, and CK20) and the suspected ‘clear cells’ were negative for CK, CK7, and CK20, which ruled out the diagnosis of RCC. The ‘foam cells’ consistent with XGPN were first misinterpreted as malignant ‘clear cells’. The immunohistochemistry study was essential to rule out malignancy and confirmed the diagnosis of XGPN. CD68 was not available in our pathology lab.

in_text_mentions: Histopathological examination by Hematoxylin and Eosin stain (H&E) revealed xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis with extensive ischaemic necrosis. The pathognomonic microscopic feature is the lipid-laden foamy macrophage accompanied by both chronic- and acute-phase inflammatory cells as shown in the Figures 5-7. Real-time tuberculosis-polymerase chain reaction (TB-PCR) test was negative. Tissue culture showed no growth.

plate_findings.evidence: inflammatory infiltrate rich in xanthemous foam cells

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Real patient H&E histology (×20) of the resected renal lesion showing granulomatous inflammation with cholesterol crystals, characteristic of xanthogranulomatous inflammation. The article text confirms Fig. 3 is the histopathology of the lesion diagnosed as pseudotumoral Xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis. Cholesterol crystals/granulomatous reaction are present but not in the allowed vocabulary, so they are listed as proposed findings. B: Real patient H&E histology (×40) showing an inflammatory infiltrate rich in foamy xanthoma cells, the classic histologic hallmark of xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis, from the lesion the article text identifies as pseudotumoral XPN. Direct caption evidence and confirmed disease attribution.
panels.attribution_text: Saadi et al. Xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis presenting as a cystic mass: a rare case report.. Journal of surgical case reports 2021. doi:10.1093/jscr/rjab265. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: histological examination. (A) Hematoxylin Eosin × 20: inflammatory granulomatous changes in contact with cholesterol crystals. (B) Hematoxylin Eosin × 40: inflammatory infiltrate rich in xanthemous foam cells.
in_text_mentions: nnati, OH, USA). After confirming the lack of active bleeding, we placed a drainage tube and closed the incision. The total operation time was 1 h 45 min, with 18 min of selective clamping. The post-operative course was uneventful, and the patient was discharged 2 days post-operatively. The histopathological examination revealed a 2.5 × 2.7 cm necrotic lesion with an inflammatory interstitial infiltrate dissociating the epithelial structures (Fig. 3). The retained diagnosis was a pseudo tumoral Xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis. The CT performed 3-months after surgery showed no abnormalities.

in_text_mentions: Due to the presence of a mass, a CT-guided renal mass biopsy was done, which showed linear cores of renal tissue with viable and intact glomeruli. Interstitium showed moderate infiltration of mixed inflammatory cells comprising of lymphocytes, plasma cells, mainly histiocytes, eosinophils, and some neutrophils. Focal area of necrosis was also present. In some areas, lymphocytes and neutrophils were seen invading the tubular epithelium, and neutrophilic cast was noted within the tubular lumen (Figure 2).

panels.rationale: Single gross pathology panel (A) of a right radical nephrectomy specimen from a human patient. The article is disease-focused on xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis, and the caption documents an enlarged kidney (11.2 × 6.5 × 4.5 cm) with congested Gerota fascia and a blue-arrowhead-marked low-density lesion; the cut surface shows diffuse golden-yellow xanthomatous nodular replacement with distorted architecture and perinephric inflammatory extension—classic gross features of XGP. Real patient specimen image, no third-party copyright.

panels.figure_caption: Pathology. Grossly, the Gerota fascia was congested, and the kidney was 11.2 × 6.5 × 4.5 cm in size. The low-density lesion (3.3 × 3.1 × 3.0 cm in size) was marked by a blue arrowhead.
in_text_mentions: uspected renal tumor. After discussing with the patient and her family, right open radical nephrectomy was performed. The final pathology report was MKP, the Gerota fascia was congested, and the kidney was 11.2 × 6.5 × 4.5 cm in size (Fig. 2) with marked foamy macrophages, lymphoplasmacytic cells and neutrophil infiltrate in the kidney, ureter, and perirenal fat (Fig. 3). After the surgical treatment, her clinical recovery and laboratory outcomes were satisfactory, and she has no longer suffered from urosepsis for many years. There were no adverse event or recurrence noted on follow-up images.

panels.rationale: Real human abdominal plain radiograph from a disease-focused article on xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis with calculus migration. The image visibly shows a large branched radio-opaque shadow in the left renal fossa (staghorn-type calculus) plus smaller pelvic opacities, matching the captioned multiple calculi. Staghorn calculus is a classic, well-recognized manifestation of XGP, so the panel qualifies; attribution relies on the disease-focused article title plus the specific captioned manifestation. No age, ethnicity, or skin findings are applicable.

panels.rationale: Single axial non-contrast abdominal CT from an article specifically about infliximab-associated xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis. The in-text explicitly ties this figure to a heterogeneous hypodense soft tissue mass in the left lower kidney with multiple abscesses, i.e. XGP-type cavitary destruction with a mass-like renal replacement. The caption additionally notes horseshoe kidneys, which is a congenital predisposing anomaly rather than an XGP manifestation and is therefore not tagged as a disease finding. Disease attribution rests on the disease-focused title together with specific in-text imaging findings; the single non-contrast slice limits direct visual confirmation of the abscesses, so confidence is moderate.

panels.rationale: Coronal contrast CT of the abdomen from a real patient with xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis (article title and primary disease key). Red arrows mark inferior lateral renal nodular densities along the renal fascia; the in-text describes nodular implants posterior and lateral to the right kidney and along the paracolic gutter that may represent extension of the renal process, matching perirenal inflammatory extension. Blue arrows mark subscapular hepatic hypodensities (perihepatic nodular implants with perihepatic ascites), consistent with contiguous inflammatory extension. Annotated image with no third-party restriction. Confidence tempered by the coexisting primary renal squamous cell carcinoma, which raises some ambiguity with peritoneal carcinomatosis, but the caption, in-text and prior triage attribute the findings to XPN extension.

panels.rationale: Coronal contrast CT of the abdomen in a patient whose imaging is presented as xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis (disease-focused article title plus in-text XGP features). The right kidney shows marked hydronephrosis with multiple dilated/cavitary calyces containing air locules, perirenal inflammation, and a pyelogastric fistula (blue arrow) linking upper renal calculi to the gastric antrum (red arrows mark air). These are specific radiographic manifestations of XGP; the pyelogastric fistula is a rare complication, hence atypical. The fistula, air locules and non-staghorn renal calculi are not covered by the allowed vocabulary and are listed as proposed findings. No age, ethnicity or skin assessment is applicable/stated.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (1A, 1B). 1A: Non-contrast CT from a case report titled xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis mimicking a complex renal cyst; caption describes a large heterogeneous renal lesion with septations, supporting XGP-related renal distortion/cavitation. The lesion is atypical because it mimics a complex renal cyst. 1B: Contrast-enhanced CT from the same case report; caption states no significant enhancement of the large lesion, consistent with the XGP case description. Marked as atypical because the mass was reported to mimic a complex renal cyst.

No significant contrast enhancement was noted.

plate_findings.evidence: large well-defined ... mass lesion measuring ~ 10x9x9 cms ... arising from the mid pole of the right kidney

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Axial T1-weighted MRI shows a large right renal mass with hyperintense/hemorrhagic areas, in a case report of xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis; the article title and in-text context support disease attribution, though the caption notes the findings are not pathognomonic. B: Axial T2-weighted MRI shows a large heterogeneous right renal mass, corresponding to the XGPN case described; findings are not pathognomonic, but the article title and in-text discussion link the mass to xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis.
panels.attribution_text: Chandrashekhar et al. Xanthogranulomatous Pyelonephritis Mimicking a Complex Renal Cyst: A Report of a Rare Case.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.69233. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: MRI images (A) A right renal lesion with multiple areas of GRE blooming, which appears hyperintense on T1 and (B) large, well-defined, heterogeneously hyperintense right renal mass on T2 weighted imaging.
in_text_mentions: As depicted in Figure 2, MRI revealed a large well-defined T2 heterogeneously hyperintense and T1 heterogeneously isointense mass lesion measuring ~ 10x9x9 cms (CC x AP x TR) arising from the mid pole of the right kidney, which showed few subtle areas of restricted diffusion and multiple areas of GRE blooming which appeared hyperintense on T1, suggestive of hemorrhagic areas. While these imaging findings are not pathognomonic for XGPN, hemorrhagic areas could be due to granulation tissue seen in XGPN [3].

panels.rationale: Single axial CT of the abdomen in a patient with a disease-focused title on xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis (the right renal process; the left kidney is explicitly normal). The blue-arrow posterior-lateral nodular density of the right kidney is tied in the text to extension of the renal process, supporting perirenal inflammatory extension of xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis; no classic bear's-paw sign or central staghorn calculus is described, and the case is framed as very rare, so the presentation is atypical. The red-arrow renal vein/artery filling defect and yellow-arrow gastric air-fluid level are clearly present but are not xanthogranulomatous-pyelonephritis vocabulary findings (listed as proposed). Because the same case concerns a primary renal squamous cell carcinoma and the text calls the perirenal densities 'implants' (a term that can imply tumor deposits) with only a tentative ('may be related') link to the renal process, disease attribution is not fully certain, giving moderate confidence.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: Axial contrast CT of a real patient showing gas within the left renal collecting system calices with dilated calyces; the article title and in-text explicitly attribute the findings to XPN complicated by emphysematous pyelonephritis, so the intrarenal gas is a direct manifestation of the configured disease in this case. [raw subtype: emphysematous] b: Axial contrast CT of a real patient showing a large 3.3 cm stone within the left renal pelvis with dilated calices; central renal pelvis calculus with calyceal dilation is a textbook CT manifestation of XPN, and the in-text explicitly attributes the findings to XPN.

in_text_mentions: An initial chest x-ray demonstrated no acute cardiopulmonary process. CT abdomen and pelvis revealed severe hydronephrosis and dilated calices of the left kidney with a 3.3 cm stone within the left renal pelvis along with stones in the lower poles of the left kidney. There was also gas within the left renal collecting system in the calices (Figures 1 and 2). The findings were concerning for XPN with emphysematous. The patient was transferred to inpatient care and treated with ceftriaxone 2.0 g IV q 24 h.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Clinical photograph of a 5x5 cm soft right flank mass in an 89-year-old woman; the article title ('an unusual cause of a right flank mass') and in-text examination attribute this flank mass to xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis. Real patient image showing a clinical manifestation of the target disease; the flank mass is not in the allowed vocabulary so it is recorded as a proposed finding. B: Axial contrast CT of the same XPG patient, captioned as right stage III XPG (asterisk) with renal abscess (diamond), rim-enhancing cystic structures and perinephric fat stranding. These are characteristic CT manifestations of xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis with perirenal inflammatory extension. C: Sagittal CT of the same patient captioned with stage III XPG (asterisk) and renal abscess (diamond) herniating through the posterior abdominal wall, i.e. cavitary renal destruction with perirenal/posterior abdominal wall extension of...

International braz j urol : official journal of the Brazilian Society of Urology 2021. doi:10.1590/s1677-5538.ibju.2020.0641. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: An 89 year-old female presenting with functional decline and a fall was discovered to have a right flank mass. She underwent CT abdomen and pelvis to evaluate the flank mass.
in_text_mentions: Past medical history was significant for well-controlled hypertension, osteoporosis, and cognitive impairment. She was febrile (temperature 38 degrees Celsius), blood pressure 110mmHg/80mmHg, pulse rate 85 beats per minute, saturating 100% on ambient air. Physical examination revealed a 5x5cm soft, right flank mass protruding from the posterolateral aspect of the right flank (Figure-1A).

more extensively into the retroperitoneum and herniated through the posterior abdominal wall (stage III XPG), with concomitant renal abscess. Rim-enhancement of these cystic structures with surrounding mild fat stranding was seen, representing acute superimposed infection (Figure-1B, Axial View of the CT scan: white asterisk representing right sided stage III XPG, white diamond representing the renal abscess herniating through the posterior abdominal wall, Figure-1C, Sagittal View of the CT scan: white asterisk representing right sided stage III XPG, white diamond representing renal abscess).

for the right renal abscess located at the right inferior renal pole respectively. Fluid culture revealed Streptococcus anginosus. Cytology was compatible with acute suppurative inflammation. Urine culture revealed no growth. The drain was removed subsequently after a CT urogram confirmed near resolution of the collections. The excretory phase of the CT urogram confirmed that there was no passage of contrast through the renal abscess (Figure-1D). The patient remained stable and was eventually discharged with a one-month course of oral co-amoxiclav. There was no recurrence of the renal abscess.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: H&E of the nephrectomy specimen (kidney/ureter/perirenal fat) showing sheets of foamy xanthoma cells with lymphoplasmacytic and neutrophilic infiltrate and perirenal extension, the textbook microscopic picture of xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis in a case report whose title pairs malakoplakia with XGP and whose triage route is keep. B: Prussian-blue iron stain of the same human nephrectomy/ureter tissue showing scattered ferric iron granules (arrow). It is a supporting special stain of the XGP/malakoplakia case rather than a stand-alone classic XGP manifestation, so it is retained as part of the complete figure with reduced confidence. C: Von Kossa calcium stain of the same patient tissue showing numerous black calcium deposits (arrowed). Like panel B it is a supportive histologic special stain of the XGP/malakoplakia nephrectomy case, not a classic XGP manifestation by itself, so included within the complete compound figure at reduced...
panels.attribution_text: Pan et al. Malakoplakia and xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis treated with nephrectomy: A case report.. Medicine 2021. doi:10.1097/md.0000000000027137. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Pathology. (A) H&E stain. Microscopically, the kidney and ureter show a picture of MKP with marked foamy macrophage, lymphoplasmacytic cell and neutrophil infiltrate in the kidney, ureter, and perirenal fat. (B) Iron stain, is intended for use in the detection of ferric iron in tissues, blood smears, or bone marrow smears. (C) Von Kossa stain, is widely used in histology to detect the presence of abnormal calcium deposits in the body. MKP = malakoplakia.
in_text_mentions: uspected renal tumor. After discussing with the patient and her family, right open radical nephrectomy was performed. The final pathology report was MKP, the Gerota fascia was congested, and the kidney was 11.2 × 6.5 × 4.5 cm in size (Fig. 2) with marked foamy macrophages, lymphoplasmacytic cells and neutrophil infiltrate in the kidney, ureter, and perirenal fat (Fig. 3). After the surgical treatment, her clinical recovery and laboratory outcomes were satisfactory, and she has no longer suffered from urosepsis for many years. There were no adverse event or recurrence noted on follow-up images.

source_variant.figure_caption: Pathology. (A) H&E stain. Microscopically, the kidney and ureter show a picture of MKP with marked foamy macrophage, lymphoplasmacytic cell and neutrophil infiltrate in the kidney, ureter, and perirenal fat. (B) Iron stain, is intended for use in the detection of ferric iron in tissues, blood smears, or bone marrow smears. (C) Von Kossa stain, is widely used in histology to detect the presence of abnormal calcium deposits in the body. MKP = malakoplakia.
